evidence.text: Test fresh matched specimens in both flow directions and counterbalance the order. The Saffire-I directions were tested in sequence on one specimen.
The rover fan selects the concurrent orbital reference. The cabin model applies its measured speed to the strip.
Compare how far the front travels and how much oxygen is left. The cabin calculation starts with the speed you give it.

evidence.label: Cabin-physics method shown by the instrument
evidence.text:
The rigid chamber starts at 300 K with oxygen and a nitrogen balance. Each burned fuel unit consumes its stoichiometric oxygen, forming carbon dioxide and water vapor. All gas percentages use the updated total mole count. Released heat is the fuel consumed times its net heat of combustion, plus battery heat limited by available watt-hours. The model omits leaks, condensation, smoke, incomplete combustion, thermal runaway and wall heat transfer.
Surface gravity changes chassis weight and the displayed buoyant velocity scale. Real flame propagation also depends on flow, material and gravity. The chamber balance uses the front speed you enter. The Mars setting has lower confidence for transferring a surface-fire interpretation. Neither setting has experimental calibration here.
